# Overview

This project includes all necessary scripts and documentation to create the Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database (eGRID) particulate matter (PM~2.5~), ammonia (NH~3~), and volatile organic compound (VOC) emission estimates.

# Background

eGRID is a comprehensive source of data from [EPA's Clean Air and Power Division (CAPD)](https://epa.gov/power-sector) on the environmental characteristics of almost all electric power generated in the United States. Currently, eGRID includes emissions data on carbon dioxide (CO~2~), nitrogen oxides (NO~X~), sulfur dioxide (SO~2~), methane (CH~4~), and nitrous oxide (N~2~O), but does not include PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions. The data used for emission calculations in eGRID is not available for PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOCs and is instead collected from the National Emissions Inventory (NEI).

Here we use NEI data to determine PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions and emission rates as well as estimations for units that may not report to the NEI.

The final emissions datasets include four levels of data aggregation:

-   **Unit**: A set of equipment that either produces electricity and is connected to the U.S electricity grid or a set of equipment that is connected to a generator which produces electricity and is connected to the U.S. electricity grid.

-   **Plant**: A facility with one or more units and/or generators that provide power to the electric grid.

-   **State**: U.S. states, Puerto Rico (PR), and the District of Columbia (DC).

-   **eGRID subregion**: EPA defined subregions designed to limit the impacts of the import and export of electricity.

-   **National U.S.**: Contains all 50 states, Puerto Rico (PR), and the District of Columbia (DC).

Further information on the eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC methodology can be found in the [Particulate Matter Emissions for eGRID2021](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-06/egrid2021-draft-pm-memo.pdf).

The dataset that this code produces is publicly available [here](https://www.epa.gov/egrid/egrid-pm25).

## Using the .qmd file

This is a Quarto (.qmd) file that documents and runs the code necessary to create the eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC datasets. This document can be used in two ways: First, when used within an IDE, such as RStudio, it serves as an enhanced master script, allowing users to easily perform each step necessary to create the eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC data from within a single file.

Second, when viewing as a rendered file, it provides thorough documentation of the steps involved in creating the emissions data. When rendered, this file provides additional information and tools for navigating the project. The table of contents provides both a convenient look at the project structure and method for navigating the document. There are also hidden code chunks throughout, marked by a button ("Code" with an arrow next to it). Clicking this button reveals the underlying code from the R script that is being sourced in a given section. Some of the code included in this document is from the eGRID production model while the main infrastructure is specific to PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emission calculations.

## Data availability

Emissions data and crosswalks used in these calculations are from a version of EPA's NEI that are not publicly available and are therefore not included in this document. Information about the data inputs and the code used to produce the final data are included here to document the process and inform any need for replication. Meanwhile, those that do have access to the data inputs can use this document to produce the eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions datasets.

# Install Libraries and Set Parameters

Before loading any data or beginning to construct the eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions datasets, we install all necessary libraries used in subsequent scripts. Next, the eGRID year is defined, which controls which year of data is loaded from the raw data sources.

## Install required libraries

The script `install_libraries.R` detects all necessary libraries within the project using `renv::dependencies()`, checks for installation, and installs (if needed) and loads into the workspace.

```{r}
#| label: install-libraries.R
#| file: "scripts/1_production_model/install_libraries.R"
#| echo: false
```

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

library(docstring)
library(dplyr)
library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(kableExtra)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
```

## Define eGRID year

The year of eGRID specified as the parameter "eGRID_year" within the YAML of the Quarto document. When a year value needs to be specified (e.g., when pulling relevant data from the EIA API), it is done so by calling `params$eGRID_year`.

**Current year setting: `r params$eGRID_year`**

There are a set of helper functions used throughout the project. These are defined in the folder `/scripts/functions`. The `docstring` package is used to provide documentation for functions, similar to typical package documentation. To view the documentation for a given function, run `docstring({function_name})`

```{r}
functions <- list.files("scripts/functions")

```

# Input Data

## NEI

NEI provides emission estimates for PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC pollutants using the Emissions Inventory System (EIS) that aggregates pollutant data from a variety of state, local, and tribal data sources. A version of this data is provided to us annually while a publicly-available version is released every three years. You can [read more](https://www.epa.gov/air-emissions-inventories/national-emissions-inventory-nei) about NEI data and [download](https://www.epa.gov/air-emissions-inventories/get-air-emissions-data-0) the publicly-available version of data.

*NOTE: The publicly-available NEI-EIA data may differ from the version used to produce the finalized eGRID PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC data.*

## EIA

The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), a part of the Department of Energy, collects and maintains energy-related data for policy making and for the public. As of 2024, the EIA API does not contain the most detailed data available, which is necessary for the construction of eGRID. More detailed data for the EIA forms used in the eGRID production model - [923](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia923/), [860](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860/), and [861](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia861/) - are available as zipped excel file downloads on the EIA website.

A portion of the EIA data used in the eGRID production model is used here. If this data has not been downloaded previously, the following code downloads and cleans the necessary EIA data. `data_load_eia.R` creates a new folder in the project folder called `/raw_data/`. The zip file for the forms are downloaded and unzipped within this new folder. Each excel file contains several sheets that serve as the raw EIA data sources used in producing the eGRID data. EIA-923 is the only form needed to produce the PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions data.

```{r}
#| label: data-load-eia
#| file: "scripts/1_production_model/data_load_eia.R"
#| error: false
#| echo: fenced
```

```{r}
}
registerS3method("knit_print", "gt_tbl", knit_print.gt, envir = asNamespace("gt"))
```


## NEI-EIA Crosswalk

EPA's Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards (OAQPS) produces an NEI-EIA crosswalk used to match the electric generating units from the NEI emissions data to the eGRID data. NEI uses EIS codes to identify units while eGRID uses Office of Regulatory Information Systems Plant (ORISPL) codes. The crosswalk matches EIS and ORISPL codes of the same unit to directly link eGRID units to their NEI emissions data if available.

*NOTE: The NEI-EIA crosswalk is not publicly available.*

```{r}
#| label: create-xwalk-summary

xwalk_path <- glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/inputs/nei_eia_crosswalk/{params$eGRID_year}/xwalk_nei_eia.csv")
nei_eia_xwalk <-
  read.csv(xwalk_path)

# Create a tibble of column names
column_names <- tibble(`Column Names` = colnames(nei_eia_xwalk))

# Create a gt table
tab_xwalk <- 
  column_names %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**NEI-EIA Crosswalk**")
    )
```

Below are the column names within the NEI-EIA Crosswalk.

#### Overview

*Click on the tab to view the NEI-EIA Crosswalk variables.*

#### NEI-EIA Crosswalk

```{r}
#| echo: false

tab_xwalk
```
:::

## Emissions Factors

EPA's AP-42 form reports emissions factors and is used in part to estimate PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC emissions. These emissions factors are specific to unit's fuel, firing type, and prime mover and when necessary, are adjusted to account for a control efficiency. Emission factors for each of the emission types are provided as static tables.

Below are the column names within the PM~2.5~ emissions factors static table and are the same within the NH~3~ and VOC tables.

```{r}
#| label: create-emissions-factors-summary

ef_pm_path <- glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/static_tables/emission_factors_pm25.csv")
efs <-
  read.csv(ef_pm_path)

# Create a tibble of column names
column_names <- tibble(`Column Names` = colnames(efs))

# Create a gt table
tab_efs <-
  column_names %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = md("**PM<sub>2.5</sub> Emisison Factors Static Table**")
  )
```

#### Overview

*Click on the tab to view the PM~2.5~ emissions factors static table variables.*

# Produce Data

## Unit Files

For each emissions type (PM~2.5~, NH~3~, and VOC), the unit file computes annual emissions and emissions rates for units and is combined with data from the eGRID production model.

For full documentation, reference the [Particulate Matter Emissions for eGRID2021](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-06/egrid2021-draft-pm-memo.pdf).

```{r}
#| label: unit-files-create
#| file: "scripts/2a_pm_nh3_voc/unit_file_create_pm_nh3_voc.R"
#| message: FALSE
```

```{r}
#| label: unit-file-table
#| include: false

unit_file_pm25 <- readr::read_rds(
           glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/unit_file_pm25.RDS"))

unit_file_nh3 <- readr::read_rds(
           glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/unit_file_nh3.RDS"))

unit_file_voc <- readr::read_rds(
           glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/unit_file_voc.RDS"))
```

## Plant Files

The plant file aggregates the unit data at the plant level using the eGRID production model dataset and calculates unadjusted and adjusted annual emissions, and input and output emissions rates.

```{r}
#| label: plant-files-create
#| file: "scripts/2a_pm_nh3_voc/plant_file_create_pm_nh3_voc.R"
#| message: FALSE
```

```{r}
#| label: plant-file-table
#| include: false

plant_file_pm25 <- readr::read_rds(
           glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/plant_file_pm25.RDS"))

plant_file_nh3 <- readr::read_rds(
           glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/plant_file_nh3.RDS"))

plant_file_voc <- readr::read_rds(

```

## Region Aggregation Files

The plant file is aggregated to calculate annual net generation, annual emissions, and output emissions rates from the plant-level data to the various aggregated levels: state (ST), eGRID subregion (SRL), and US level.

```{r}
#| label: regional-aggregation-files-create
#| file: "scripts/2a_pm_nh3_voc/region_aggregation_create_pm_nh3_voc.R"
#| message: FALSE
```

```{r}
#| label: load-reg-agg-files
#| echo: false

pm_st_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/state_aggregation_pm25.RDS"))

pm_srl_agg <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/subregion_aggregation_pm25.RDS"))

pm_us_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/us_aggregation_pm25.RDS"))

nh3_st_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/state_aggregation_nh3.RDS"))

nh3_srl_agg <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/subregion_aggregation_nh3.RDS"))

nh3_us_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/us_aggregation_nh3.RDS"))

voc_st_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/state_aggregation_voc.RDS"))

voc_srl_agg <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/subregion_aggregation_voc.RDS"))

voc_us_agg  <- read_rds(
        glue::glue("data/2a_pm_nh3_voc/outputs/{params$eGRID_year}/us_aggregation_voc.RDS"))
```

# Produce Final Datasets

For each emissions type, the data is formatted and added to the previous year's data in an Excel file that contains all five levels of data aggregation. For headers, we add descriptions and label conventions to maintain consistency with the eGRID production model. Graphs of subregion-level generation, emissions, and emission rates are included in the final file.

The final output files are:

-   `r glue::glue("egrid{params$eGRID_year}_pmemissions.xlsx")`
-   `r glue::glue("egrid{params$eGRID_year}_nh3emissions.xlsx")`
-   `r glue::glue("egrid{params$eGRID_year}_vocemissions.xlsx")`
